Let <MATH_0001> be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme. Let
<MATH_0002> be a generic point of an irreducible component of <MATH_0003>.
<STRUCT_0001>
<STRUCT_0002> Let <MATH_0004> be a torsion abelian sheaf on <MATH_0005>
whose stalk <MATH_0006> is zero.
Then <MATH_0007> is a filtered colimit of
constructible abelian sheaves <MATH_0008> such that for each <MATH_0009>
the support of <MATH_0010> is contained
in a closed subscheme not containing <MATH_0011>.
<STRUCT_0003> Let <MATH_0012> be a Noetherian ring and <MATH_0013> a sheaf
of <MATH_0014>-modules on <MATH_0015> whose stalk
<MATH_0016> is zero. Then
<MATH_0017>
is a filtered colimit of constructible sheaves of
<MATH_0018>-modules <MATH_0019> such that for each <MATH_0020>
the support of <MATH_0021> is contained in a closed subscheme
not containing <MATH_0022>.
<STRUCT_0004>

Proof of (1). We can write <MATH_0001>
with <MATH_0002> constructible abelian by
Lemma <REF_0001>.
Choose <MATH_0003>. Since <MATH_0004> is zero by assumption, we
see that there exists an <MATH_0005> such that
<MATH_0006> is zero, see
Lemma <REF_0002>.
Then <MATH_0007>
is a constructible abelian sheaf (Lemma <REF_0003>)
whose stalk at <MATH_0008> is zero.
Hence the support <MATH_0009> of <MATH_0010> is a constructible
subset of <MATH_0011> not containing <MATH_0012>. Since
<MATH_0013> is a generic point of an irreducible component of
<MATH_0014>, we see that <MATH_0015> by
Topology, Lemma <REF_0004>.
Define a new directed set <MATH_0016> by using the set <MATH_0017> with
ordering defined by the rule
<MATH_0018> is bigger or equal to <MATH_0019> if and only if <MATH_0020>.
Then the sheaves <MATH_0021> form a system over <MATH_0022>
with colimit <MATH_0023> and the proof is complete.

The proof in case (2) is exactly the same and we omit it.
